five_modules/README.md.content:
# Independent 0.8.50 downstream fixtures

Both marker types encode the same counts, with SNP `chr,pos,A,C` or DNP
`chr,pos1,pos2,AA,CC`. They are count tables, not real patient data or BAM files.
The corresponding population tables use independent, explicitly assigned
frequencies; no expected answer is derived by running the candidate.

## Contamination

Four loci have `(REF,ALT,Other)` counts `(95,5,11)`, `(100,0,0)`, `(80,20,0)`,
`(0,0,5)`. The first is retained by the new Other/total filter (`11/111 <= .1`).
The first two are homozygous under the configured ratio rules. Consequently:

- Include zeros: 2 informative sites, mean `.025`, SD `sqrt(.00125)`.
- Exclude zeros: 1 informative site, mean `.05`, SD `NA`.

The old filter `11/100 > .1` would incorrectly retain only the zero site when
used as a reference for the newly requested model.

## Prenatal CPI

Maternal minor-allele counts are 2, 3, 4 and 1 out of 100; paternal genotypes
and ALT frequencies give PI contributions 5, 2, 2 and 5. With minimum support
2, CPI at thresholds 2,3,4 is therefore 20,4,2; the median fetal fraction is
6%. With minimum 1, the new first CPI is 100 and the fraction is 5%. Minimum
5 gives no informative sites. A separate no-sites pair tests explicit NA.
The metadata variant adds an unused all-NA column to population frequencies:
this must not discard scientifically usable sites.
The mismatch variant replaces the father at maternal support 3 with a REF
homozygote: that site's PI becomes `epsilon/.25`, yielding curve products
`40*epsilon,8*epsilon,2`. This separately verifies SNP/DNP mismatch constants.

## Postnatal CPI

Nine loci test: heterozygous paternal transmission, paternal mismatch, compatible
homozygous child, opposite mother/child homozygotes, heterozygous mother,
insufficient child support, no coverage (`total_count=NA`), excess Other,
and an unassigned paternal genotype. Only the first three pass all filters.

Their PI contributions are `0.5/0.4`, `epsilon/0.4`, and `1/0.6`, respectively.
The heterozygous-child selection contains the first two; the all-compatible
selection adds the third. Their obligatory paternal allele supports are 5,6,10,
which independently define the entire small threshold curve. `epsilon` is
`.001` for SNP and `.0000892303778101497` for DNP.

The optional full qualification copies these explicit fixtures to distinct
sample identities to test 2,3,5 trios, prenatal pairs or contamination samples. Copies are only
a process/identity stress fixture; they do not represent biological replication.

Run:

```sh
python scripts/verify_five_modules.py --full --output build/qualification-0850
# CI: use the installed R/Python payload, with its hashes checked first.
python scripts/verify_five_modules.py --image "$NIPAT_RUNTIME_IMAGE" --full --output build/qualification-image
```

The verification also executes frozen upstream scripts and compares every
reference summary field. Added candidate diagnostics and PDF bytes are not
treated as scientific differences. DNP/SNP calling, native installers, and the
combined workflow executor have separate mandatory checks.

dnp_engine/README.md.content:
# Synthetic DNPcall engine fixture

These artificial data contain no participant or patient information. They test
packaging and execution, not scientific or clinical validity.

`reference.fa` contains one 300-base synthetic contig (`chrDnpSynthetic`). Its
background bases were generated with Python `random.Random(505).choice("ACGT")`,
then the three declared REF dinucleotides were substituted at positions 50–51,
140–141 and 230–231. `DNP_list.txt` deliberately uses lowercase allele letters
to exercise normalization before passing the panel to the unchanged R script.

Each of `reads_A.sam` and `reads_B.sam` contains 63 coordinate-sorted, unpaired,
62-base reads with unique QNAMEs, mapping quality 60, base quality 40 and `62M`
alignments. Both strand flags occur. SAM sequences are already in alignment
orientation. Each read contains the chosen central dinucleotide and 30 matching
reference bases on either side. There are no indels. The start positions are
20, 110 and 200, and names are unique across loci and samples.

The expected counts below are defined by the synthetic input design, not by
running DNPcall or its wrapper. They are committed in `expected.tsv`.

| Sample | Position | REF | ALT | Other | REF reads | ALT reads | Other reads | GT |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| A | 50 | AC | GT | AT | 20 | 0 | 1 | 0/0 |
| A | 140 | TA | CG | TG | 10 | 10 | 1 | 0/1 |
| A | 230 | GC | AT | GA | 0 | 20 | 1 | 1/1 |
| B | 50 | AC | GT | AT | 0 | 20 | 1 | 1/1 |
| B | 140 | TA | CG | TG | 12 | 8 | 1 | 0/1 |
| B | 230 | GC | AT | GA | 20 | 0 | 1 | 0/0 |

Every locus has 21 reads, of which 20 are REF/ALT. The Other fraction, 1/21,
is below the native R threshold of 0.1 that masks a genotype. The heterozygous
log-likelihood is independently known: 20 × log(0.5), approximately −13.863.
It does not depend on base quality because the model assigns probability 0.5
to either expected allele under the heterozygous genotype.

`scripts/verify_engine_package.py` uses samtools inside the tested image to
convert both SAMs to BAM and generate the FASTA index. It does not generate
BAM indexes; `mpileup -l` supports this input mode. Default base-quality filters
and BAQ remain enabled. No scientific settings are changed to fit the fixture.
GL0 and GL2 are not hardcoded from the SAM's original Q40 because BAQ can alter
qualities. All scientific table fields, including those likelihoods, must also
match an independent invocation of the unchanged packaged R interface.

The real-image checks cover the complete engine request and the public client
workflow with a project directory containing only `compose.yaml`: a single BAM,
multiple BAMs with identical original basenames in distinct folders, and a BAM
list with quoted relative paths, spaces and a UTF-8 BOM. Selection order is
deliberately reversed for the multiple-BAM tests. Sequential and parallel
results must match in every table field. Assertions cover counts, haplotypes,
genotypes, sample mappings, normalized panel/list, summary columns and PDF
presence/signatures. Single-sample runs produce five PDFs and skip UpSet;
two-sample runs produce ten PDFs. Original inputs must remain unchanged.

The source-free client checks also verify image/preparation identities, read-only
input mounts, a writable current run only, and disabled container networking.
Successful native DNPcall removes its temporary pileup and BED; the normalized
panel and BAM list in `work` remain available as execution evidence.

snp_engine/README.md.content:
# Synthetic SNPcall engine fixture

These data are artificial and contain no participant or patient information.
They test packaging and execution; they are not a domain-validation dataset.

`reference.fa` contains one 180-base synthetic contig. `reads.sam` contains 13
coordinate-sorted, unpaired, 61-base reads, each with a unique QNAME, mapping
quality 60, base quality 40, and a `61M` alignment. Both strand flags occur.
The sequence stored in each SAM record is already in alignment orientation.
Each read covers the central SNP and its two neighboring bases. Reads from
different sites have distinct names. Separate 2.0 differential cases also cover
shared names across neighboring and distant SNPs. Apart from the declared central allele, every base matches
the reference. The 30-base matching flanks avoid short-read alignment ambiguity.

The expected output is defined independently by counting the declared alleles:

| SNP | REF reads | ALT reads | Other reads | Total | REF / (REF + ALT) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| chrSynthetic:50 A>G | 4 | 2 | 1 | 7 | 4/6 |
| chrSynthetic:120 C>T | 2 | 3 | 1 | 6 | 2/5 |

`scripts/verify_engine_package.py` uses samtools in the tested image to convert
this SAM to BAM and generate the FASTA index. It deliberately does not generate
a BAM index: the supported SNPcall command selects regions with `mpileup -l`.
It uses the SNPcall 2.0 `-d 0` depth setting, retaining samtools default quality
filters and BAQ behavior. A mismatch with the counts above fails the regression;
the fixture is not used to alter the scientific settings.

The real-image check then runs the complete BAM workflow, validates the BED
windows and the retained seven-column pileup, compares every output field with
`expected.tsv` (numeric tolerance 1e-12), and repeats the analysis from that pileup
through the public Python workflow. The existing nine-site upstream pileup
example remains an additional independent regression.

The 17-column 2.0 oracle also uses each declared central Phred40 score:
`eps=10^(-40/10)`, with the sum of log probabilities under 0/0, 0/1 and
1/1. Both fixture sites have Other fractions above 10%, so GT is `NA` while
likelihoods remain available. No reads contain indels: both indel fields are
zero. `combined_bases`/`combined_counts` retain every observed allele in
alphabetical order, including T at50 and G at120. These expectations are
computed independently in `verify_snp_workflow.independent_snp_row`, then
compared with the pinned upstream core and the candidate.

# Synthetic BAM-to-CPI workflow regression

The scientific integration check generates artificial reads in
`scripts/verify_workflow_execution.py` and runs the public automatic workflow
through the packaged image. No participant or patient data are used.

The sequence contexts, reference, chromosome and three DNP positions come from
`tests/fixtures/dnp_engine`. The generator selects one REF and one ALT 62M
alignment template at each position from its committed `reads_A.sam` and
`reads_B.sam`. It preserves the aligned sequence and mapping quality 60, assigns
unique read names, alternates strand flags 0/16, and sets every base quality to
Phred 40. Alignments remain sorted by position; no indels or Other alleles are
introduced. Each generated BAM contains 300 reads and is deliberately unindexed.
The image's samtools converts SAM to BAM and indexes the synthetic FASTA.

| DNP positions | Maternal REF / ALT | Paternal REF / ALT | Other | REF / ALT population frequency |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 50–51, 140–141, 230–231 | 96 / 4 at each site | 50 / 50 at each site | 0 | 0.75 / 0.25 |

The expectations derive from these input counts, independently of the code
under test:

- All three maternal sites satisfy the homozygous-majority criterion and have
  four fetal reads. Each fetal-fraction estimate is `2 × 4 / 100 = 0.08` (8%).
- Each paternal site is heterozygous. Its paternity index is `0.5 / 0.25 = 2`.
  Across all three sites CPI is `2³ = 8`, so the log10 summaries round to
  `0.903` for every fetal-read threshold 2 through 4.
- A named panel selecting only the first site retains the same fetal fraction,
  one maternal/paternal site and log10 CPI rounded to `0.301`.
- Contamination retains all three maternal sites with `4 / 100 = 0.04` per site:
  the mean is 0.04 and the sample standard deviation is 0. The paternal sample
  has no informative contamination sites, giving count 0 and `NA` estimates.

The full preset must execute DNPcall once, then Contamination and CPI. CPI reads
DNPcall's original individual tables directly. Passing the Contamination output
instead would lose the heterozygous paternal sites and fail this oracle.

Additional checks compare every CPI CSV value with a separate execution of the
same packaged R workflow, verify PDF filenames/signatures, preserve explicit
maternal/paternal identities and input bytes, and record one container command
and distinct step states. PDF appearance is not compared.

The separate DNPcall → CPI preset uses the existing DNP fixture unchanged and
checks its expected zero-informative-site/`NA` result. Imported-table plans reuse
`tests/fixtures/cpi` and `tests/fixtures/cpi_engine` for positive numerical
regressions, shared maternal inputs, multiple pairs, ALL/single/named panels and
an error-constant-sensitive case. These are software regression checks, not
acceptance of the scientific method on real samples.
